target_name: Value Premium Flip Across Capacity Growth Regimes
rationale: The indicator algebra correctly produces +1 for near-flat capacity, −1 for >15% PPE growth, and 0 in the middle band, so the expression genuinely implements the stated sign-flip and yields a design whose spread cannot be a repackaged HML — though the value×investment interaction is adjacent to published findings that the value premium concentrates in low-investment firms, and the hard-coded absolute thresholds are unmotivated.

Internally consistent (top-30% B/M gate times negated capex/PPE z-score, long = cheap-and-restrained) and a legitimate within-value trap test, but it is close to the well-documented investment anomaly conditioned on value, and the 70% zero mass means only ~15% tails carry information, which will make decile composition thin and breakpoints degenerate.

This is essentially the archived "Expensive Empire Builder Short" mechanism (rich multiple × capex-plus-acquisition expansion) with a percentile gate and a PPE denominator substituted for assets — a construction-level variant rather than a diagnosis-driven redesign of why that signal's FMB slope and FF5 alpha disagreed in sign.

The MIN-of-ranks AND gate plus a reinvestment-deceleration (change-in-rate) leg is a genuinely non-linear, level-orthogonal construction that neither HML nor CMA spans; the main caveats are that MIN is asymmetric (the short leg is an OR mixture, so leg-matching is weaker than claimed) and that first differences of capex/ppent are noisy.

The labor-input channel is a legitimately different dimension from capex, but the construction reverts to exactly the additive SUMRANK-with-value-yield form that already delivered a strong FMB slope with a wrong-signed FF5 alpha in the archive, the productivity leg is contaminated by layoff-driven improvements, and the claim about emp coverage is optimistic given how often it is missing or stale.

target_name: Cheapness With High Return On Incremental Capex
rationale: The stated hypothesis (investment quality, orthogonal to investment level) conflicts with the mechanics: with a near-zero-capex denominator, DELTA(ebitda)/MA(capx,3) is dominated by 1/capx cross-sectionally, so the signal reloads on low investment level (CMA) rather than isolating return on incremental capital, and the additive pairing with ib/mktcap repeats the archived HML-dominated composite.
